verified.notes: Installed from the packed tarball into a disposable isolated non-Desktop profile, composed with --dump-config, booted with a bounded real startup, exercised over the authenticated /api transport, generated one real image through the live Agnes API, downloaded its bytes through the media route, verified the record and artifact survive a restart, and verified deletion removes both. The Client half was then driven in a real headless Chrome against the owned DSH Web app over CDP (scripts/ui-check.mjs), with two deterministic image records seeded into the owned data directory (scripts/seed-fixture.mjs) so the gallery and viewer could be exercised without network, credentials or quota: the sidebar entry selects the studio page, the panel renders without a console error, the two-pane body is measured to be two columns side by side with the composer pinned to the left edge of the content column and the gallery taking the remaining width, the parameter controls render their model-derived values in the shape their option count calls for (a segmented control for four resolutions, chips for eight ratios), the Flash video model narrows the resolution list to 720P, the generate button is measured to sit inside the viewport rather than below the fold, a disabled primary is verified to drop the gradient and stay opaque, the gallery renders its cards in a uniform 4:3 crop, the category filter is verified to change the rendered results, both themes are measured to change the panel's surface and text colours, the prompt optimizer is verified present inside the prompt box, an idle panel is verified to show no phantom in-flight UI, a retry is verified to render its progress inside the failed record's own card after a full page reload (exactly one retrying card, zero placeholder cards, no duplicated background banner, the card count unchanged), and that attempt is followed through a real generation until it settles back into the same record, and the image viewer opens in-panel, covers the whole viewport with no containing-block trap, zooms by a measured layout change rather than a label, closes on Escape and on a backdrop click, does not close when the picture itself is clicked, steps through the gallery with the arrow keys while resetting the zoom per picture, and returns focus to the control that opened it. The suite was run twice: keyless (exercising the unconfigured branches, including the disabled primary's flat muted surface) and with a real key (the empty-prompt refusal branch plus the two retry checks, which start a real generation and follow it into the same record). Beyond the automated suite, real-key end-to-end runs against the live API verified the background-job and retry behaviours that cannot be asserted offline: a submitted image kept rendering after the panel was left and was still shown as running on return before settling into a result card; a failed video record retried successfully after a FULL page reload, with the card count unchanged (the row is updated in place); clicking retry on a failed record showed the progress only inside that card (no extra placeholder card, no background banner), and the same record then turned into the generated result in its original slot with the card count unchanged; and the prompt optimizer rewrote a draft and the undo restored the original text. Evidence: docs/evidence/isolated-mount-0.5.1.json, docs/evidence/browser-ui-check.json and docs/evidence/screenshots/. Cleanup verified: owned roots removed, all processes stopped. A finished picture can be continued: the panel restores its exact request, shows the source thumbnail, and submits the stored picture as the next request's reference — the Host inlines the bytes it already owns as a data: URI because the upstream cannot reach the authenticated same-origin media route. The browser suite therefore clicks 继续编辑 on a seeded picture, asserts the prompt came back, the source thumbnail is shown, the card count is unchanged and the submit button reads 生成修改版, then submits and follows a REAL data: URI image-to-image generation until the new version settles INTO the original's stack (card count unchanged) carrying its 承接 lineage, and finally reads the owned store to prove the new record keeps the symbolic reference and derivedFrom instead of freezing base64 into the index. A failed record instead restores only its prompt and parameters (调整后重试), which the offline suite covers for both capabilities; a finished video deliberately offers no continuation, because upstream has no video edit/extension endpoint and its reference-video input needs a public URL on the paid model. A continuation now JOINS its source instead of adding a sibling: the gallery groups records into lineages by derivedFrom, renders one stacked card per lineage with the newest version on top and up to two peeking layers behind it, and labels it with a version badge. The browser suite therefore asserts that a settled continuation leaves the card count UNCHANGED, produces exactly one stack with at least one peeking layer, shows a two-version badge and keeps the 承接 lineage on the top card; it then sweeps a REAL mouse down the picture through seven positions and requires the card's and the picture's getBoundingClientRect to be IDENTICAL at every one — the machine-checkable form of the reported flashing and shaking, which a jsdom test cannot measure — while requiring the sweep to genuinely reach the older version, then verifies leaving the stack restores the newest version; it then clicks the version rail to PIN the older version and verifies the badge and rail follow, the pin survives the pointer leaving, the card height is unchanged, and clicking "1" returns to following the newest version; it then re-renders the stack in the OTHER theme and verifies the peeking sliver is still painting its picture and is not transparent (the early theme screenshot is taken before any stack exists, so this is the only place the dark stack is ever looked at); finally it clicks 展开 and verifies every version becomes its own card, then 收起 and verifies the stack returns. A deep six-version lineage is then seeded and the page reloaded: the version rail must list six numbers with none clipped out of its box, the peek budget must stay capped at two, the badge must report six versions, the rail must reach the oldest version, and a real scrub across the six-version picture must keep the card's measured box identical — the geometry guarantees must hold for a real editing chain, not only for a chain of two. Scrubbing is deliberately scoped to the picture, not the action row, so a card cannot change identity under a pointer that is about to click one of its buttons. Continuous retry is Host-owned: a retryable failure optionally starts a background loop with exponential backoff (15s doubling to a 180s cap, 5 attempts by default) that survives the panel being closed and reports its attempt number and next-attempt time through state(); only self-healing failures (queue full, rate limit, 5xx, timeout, broken download) are retried, a deterministic refusal is reported after one try, and the loop writes exactly one final record carrying its attempt count. The stack itself was rewritten for interaction quality after the first release shook under the pointer: every version's picture and body stay MOUNTED (so a version change is an opacity crossfade, never a remount that would drop the decode and reset the hover transition), all bodies share ONE grid cell (so the card is always as tall as its tallest version and scrubbing cannot change its height), the picture is a fixed 4:3 box, the front card does not run the generic hover lift or the generic thumbnail zoom/veil (a transform under a scrubbing pointer is exactly the wobble being fixed; the veil covered the gesture region), the peeking layers carry the BACK versions' own cropped pictures and never repeat the version already on the face of the stack, hidden shots and bodies are visibility:hidden rather than removed (keeping the geometry while leaving the hit test, tab order and accessibility tree), and stack shots load eagerly rather than lazily so the first flip never fades into an undecoded frame. Operability was added alongside it: a numbered version rail commits to a version (its own view/download/edit/delete actions become the card's, and the pin survives the pointer leaving), the picture advertises the vertical gesture with an ns-resize cursor and a hover hint that retires once the user has actually scrubbed, and the rail is the only control on touch devices, which have no hover.
